clue.text: Part of his stock is made the wrong way

definitions.text: Part of his stock is made the wrong way

parts.words: Part of his stock is made the wrong way
parts.note: the word made spelt backwards gives a Dutch cheese, which this trader keeps on his shelves

explanation.surface: Some goods in a shop have been badly manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made the wrong way' looks like shoddy workmanship, but read 'made' backwards to get EDAM, a cheese, and ask whose stock includes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in Edam and other dairy produce keeps it among his wares.

clue.text: American city's elegant past

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A US city is said to have had a stylish history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illinois metropolis on Lake Michigan is a major city of the United States.

clue.text: Manage to rise above Henry, starting a new era

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed above another comes first
in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to cope is to manage
Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in outdoing a man called Henry and so begins a fresh age.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous enough to open a fresh period of history is called that.

clue.text: Seen perhaps to have the odour of venerability ?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of the word seen could be arranged some other way

parts.note: a scent is an odour

explanation.surface: Something seen seems to give off the smell of old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SEEN into SENE, followed by SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing old describes the state of age that venerability implies.

clue.text: Old Goldfinger

parts.note: the Bond villain's name read literally is someone whose fingers turned things to gold, a legendary ancient king

explanation.surface: A reference to the veteran Bond villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldfinger suggests the James Bond film; read literally it is the king of Phrygian myth whose touch turned everything to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical king of Phrygia was granted a golden touch, so he was the original golden finger.

clue.text: Carp right not to take the whole bait?

definitions.text: not to take the whole bait?

parts.note: to carp is to find fault, to nibble at someone

explanation.surface: A carp is reluctant to swallow the angler's lure entire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish, but it is the verb meaning to criticise pettily.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish that only takes small bites at a hook is a taster rather than a swallower.

clue.text: Gladstone, for one, when in form

definitions.text: Gladstone, for one, when in form

parts.words: Gladstone, for one, when in form
parts.note: the Victorian prime minister was once a pupil sitting in a class, or form, at a famous school near Windsor

explanation.surface: The statesman Gladstone at the top of his game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' suggests good condition; it means in a school class. Gladstone went to Eton, an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone was a former pupil of Eton College, the school near Windsor.

clue.text: If well cooked, I may want gull soup

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of the words are mixed and prepared afresh

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a soup made from a seabird, provided it is cooked properly.
explanation.definitionFit: This curried broth of Anglo-Indian origin is a soup.

clue.text: He was beaten and given bread. Fabulous !

definitions.text: He was beaten and given bread. Fabulous !

parts.words: He was beaten and given bread. Fabulous
parts.note: a nursery rhyme tells of a heraldic beast drummed out of town by the lion and handed white and brown bread; fabulous means mythical

explanation.surface: A man was thrashed and then fed, which is splendid news.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'The Lion and the Unicorn' says the lion beat the unicorn round the town, and some gave them white bread. 'Fabulous' means legendary, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-horned horse of legend is a fabulous creature, and the rhyme says it was beaten and fed bread.

clue.text: They may be impoverished owing to others

definitions.text: They may be impoverished owing to others

parts.words: They may be impoverished owing to others
parts.note: people who owe money to others may be left poor by it, the literal sense of owing

explanation.surface: Some people are poor because of what other people did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'owing to' looks like 'because of'; read literally it means owing money to others.
explanation.definitionFit: People who owe money are in debt, which can leave them poor.

clue.text: Chips, for example

parts.note: Mr Chips is the gentle teacher of the novel Goodbye, Mr Chips

explanation.surface: An example of fried potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Not fried potatoes: Mr Chips is the old teacher in James Hilton's novel 'Goodbye, Mr Chips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Chips taught at a boys' school, so he is an example of a teacher.

clue.text: Leads Ayesha into the meadows

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: leas are meadows
Ayesha is the immortal queen in Rider Haggard's novel She

explanation.surface: Someone guides a woman named Ayesha into the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayesha is the title figure of H. Rider Haggard's 'She', so she gives SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog leads are straps for walking a pet, also called by this word.

clue.text: Inconsiderate to trade in seafood, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and only its sound matters

parts.note: to sell fish is to trade in seafood

explanation.surface: Running a fish business is described as thoughtless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thinking only of themselves is careless of others' feelings.

clue.text: Demon of a troubled lough

indicators.note: troubled water is stirred up, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A monster from a stormy Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit that robs graves is a kind of demon.

clue.text: Such language by an optimist

parts.note: the invented international tongue takes its name from its creator's pen name, meaning one who hopes

explanation.surface: Hopeful talk from a cheerful person.
explanation.walkthrough: Zamenhof published his invented language under the pen name Doktoro Esperanto, 'one who hopes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The artificial world language was named from a word for a hopeful person.

clue.text: " More needs she the divine than the" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: More needs she the divine than the

parts.words: More needs she the divine than the
parts.note: the line from Macbeth ends with a word for a doctor, contrasted with the priest Lady Macbeth needs

explanation.surface: A line from Macbeth with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doctor in Macbeth says Lady Macbeth needs a priest more than a medical man; fill in the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor in Macbeth says this of himself: a medical man is less use to her than a priest.

clue.text: Wireless communication one has in mind?

definitions.text: Wireless communication one has in mind?

parts.words: Wireless communication one has in mind?
parts.note: wireless suggests radio, but read literally it is contact without wires, made from mind to mind

explanation.surface: What sort of radio contact is someone thinking of?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wireless' is an old British word for radio; here it means without any wires at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought transference passes messages between minds with no physical link.

clue.text: State of Christmas rising about prohibition

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other
in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: Noel is Christmas
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Something about the festive season goes up despite a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NOEL into LEON, which goes 'about' BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern republic on the Mediterranean is a country, or state.

clue.text: A ward of Paris ?

parts.note: a ward of Paris suggests a district of the city, but means a person under protection, with a French word

explanation.surface: Asking about a district of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris has numbered districts, but here 'ward' means someone in another's care, and 'of Paris' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for someone protected and guided by a patron means a ward.

clue.text: Place held by a relief doctor

definitions.text: Place held by a relief doctor

parts.words: Place held by a relief doctor
parts.note: the Latin full form of the title means holding the place, as a stand-in doctor does

explanation.surface: A post occupied by a doctor covering for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is short for Latin 'locum tenens', 'holding the place'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in doctor holds another's place, which is what the Latin phrase means.

clue.text: Girl in " Salad Days ", do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear signals that a word sounds like another

parts.note: lettuce is the basic salad leaf

explanation.surface: A girl in the musical Salad Days, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: Salad Days is a 1950s British musical; the salad leaf sounds like the old girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned name was given to girls.

clue.text: Agreement to keep the powder dry

definitions.meaning: a pact or treaty between parties
a small hinged case for carrying face powder

explanation.surface: A deal made so that the gunpowder stays dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep the powder dry' suggests the old military saying about gunpowder; it is face powder in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is called by this word, and so is a small case holding face powder.

clue.text: To make new brew, mow with Us caterpillar

indicators.note: making something new means the letters are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone mows while brewing a fresh batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' stands for US, as printed in the old paper: an American caterpillar.
explanation.definitionFit: An American moth larva that spins webs over leaves is so called.

clue.text: Noted contribution to Orsino's love-feast

parts.note: Orsino opens Twelfth Night calling for more if it is the food of love; noted means made of notes

explanation.surface: A famous dish brought to Orsino's romantic banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night opens: 'If music be the food of love, play on.' 'Noted' means made of musical notes, not famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino treats sound in notes as the food of love.

clue.text: What a neck the Corinthians had !

definitions.text: What a neck the Corinthians had !

parts.words: What a neck the Corinthians had
parts.note: neck suggests cheek, but means a narrow strip of land, such as the one at Corinth

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at the cheek of the people of Corinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a neck' sounds like 'what a nerve'; it means a land neck. Corinth stands on the narrow strip joining the Peloponnese to mainland Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow neck of land joining two larger masses, like that at Corinth.

clue.text: Could be NE York's satellite? No, New York's

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters might form another word

parts.note: the letters of NE and York's, with the S

explanation.surface: Is this a town near York in northern England? No, it is near New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters do not make a place near York, England, but a city just north of New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Westchester County borders the Bronx, a satellite of New York City.

clue.text: In one board meeting conclusion it provides copy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: In says the following word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a chess game is a meeting over a board, and mate is how it ends

explanation.surface: At the end of a company board meeting, a document is copied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' suggests directors; it is a chess game, which ends in MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce or mimic something is to make a copy of it.

clue.text: Join together to bury associate

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to connect is to associate

explanation.surface: Someone seeks to unite in order to bury a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To link things with each other is to join them together.
